newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Majors hit mogas price.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Majors hit mogas price.

text.p: Naphtha prices were unchanged on Thursday amid a lack of any strong direction, while gasoline edged down under the pressure of fresh supplies.
Singapore weekly gasoline, reformate and naphtha stocks only rose marginally by 27,000 barrels to 5.207 million barrels.

A European trader, who has already sold more than half a million barrels of gasoline in the past week, re-appeared to sell 50,000 barrels of 97-octane to a Japanese trader - who has already bought around 450,000 barrels in the past week - at $28.65 per barrel, fob Singapore lifting April 6-10.
The major had sold 97-octane on Wednesday at $28.85 to a Dutch trader for April 8-12 lifting.
Another major - from the U.S. - emerged to offer 95- and 92-octane at $28.45 and $28.00 respectively. The cargoes failed to attract buyers.

Traders said levels were easily led down by crude as bearish sentiment has crept into the market after Taiwan's low reformate purchase award on Wednesday of $28.60 c-and-f and the expected return of the 125,000-bpd Dumai refinery in Indonesia on March 21.

But on a more bullish note, Vietnam National Petroleum Import-Export Corp (Petrolimex) is seeking 144,000 tonnes of gasoline in its tender for April-June deliveries when compared with first quarter purchases by tender of 85,000 tonnes and a subsequent spot purchase of 17-18,000 tonnes.
The latest tender closes March 28 and is valid until April 5. It seeks 83-octane gasoline with a lead content of 0.15 grammes per litre.
Naphtha held steady in the absence of any direction from Japan, which was closed for a day's holiday on Thursday.
April swaps were last quoted at $24.30/$24.40 per barrel, compared to $24.20/$24.60.
Traders in Singapore said April naphtha fob cargoes were mostly committed at more than $1.00 to $1.40 per barrel over spot quotes. Demand for May was yet to emerge.
But they were still eyeing possible arbitrage cargoes from the Mediterranean and Northwest Europe with the wide East-West spread.
"The West is weak...April is very much oversupplied," said one western trader.
He said the first-half May open-spec/April NWE spread has widened to around $32 per tonne, from around $23 two weeks ago.

Reflecting the high prices in Asia, Petron in the Philippines sold a spot full-range cargo of 200-220,000 barrels late last week at $3.00 over Japanese spot quotes fob Bataan. The spot sale, to a Japanese trader, was much higher than Petron's 1997 term price of $2 under Japanese quotes, traders said.

But Sri Lanka's state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corp (CPC) sold by tender 110,000-125,000 barrels of March 24-25 light naphtha to Japanese trader Tomen at 88 cents per barrel below Singapore quotes, fob Colombo, a company official said.
CPC last sold 25,000 tonnes of naphtha at 73 cents below Singapore quotes lifting January 20-21, fob Colombo.
"The price is lower than the last award because the tender was on short notice.. the cargo loads next week," the official explained.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
